tagline: A short Coast Range road with a falls halfway along.
intro: From Alsea on Route 34 the byway goes up the South Fork of the Alsea into the Coast Range, beside a river of rapids and pools. Douglas fir and vine maple cover the hills along the way, and old-growth fir and western red cedar stand on the ridges near the falls. The road comes out at Alpine, west of Monroe.
It is a short road, about half an hour by the federal reckoning, and there is no cell signal in the drainage.

moments.title: Alsea
moments.text: Settlers came over from the Willamette Valley in the 1850s to take up land claims, and a place that once lived by logging is known now for its steelhead fishing.

moments.title: Alsea Falls
moments.text: In the day-use area the South Fork cascades 30 feet over rock, with trails wandering off through the trees to the picnic grounds.

moments.title: Alpine
moments.text: A railroad begun in 1908 ended here when the money did, atop the foothill that named the place, though it has been noted that the situation is not particularly alpine in character.

sources.label: FHWA America's Byways, South Fork-Alsea River Back Country Byway
